prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: concussion. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1310; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened for a parking lot collision in which the insured's vehicle was struck while stopped. The claimant reports a concussion from the impact and is not represented by an attorney, so all contact is being handled directly with the claimant.

Entry 2: Reviewed the driver's listing on the policy and confirmed the driver is a named insured, with coverage active at the time of loss. Nothing in the file suggests the vehicle damage predates the coverage start.

Entry 3: Spoke with the claimant, who gave the same account of the collision as in the initial report. Police notes and two independent witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle at the time, and the other driver's statement matches.

Entry 4: Photos from the scene and the repair estimate show damage consistent with the described impact, and the injury pattern reported by the claimant fits the force of the crash. No prior injury to the same body area appears in the records available so far.

Entry 5: Treatment has continued somewhat longer than is typical for a concussion of this kind. Requested updated medical records and will review them once received. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known from prior claims or inspection notes.

Entry 6: Reviewed the full file, including the account, scene photos, witness statements, and medical history. Everything is consistent, and the claim is moving forward for evaluation of the injury and vehicle damage.
